findings.reason: the plan should name the rubric/role mechanism it extends, which is the difference between a role and a second review subsystem.
findings.text: §6 proposes `reckon/crew/figure_review.py` and `reckon/crew/prompts/figure-review.md` as new machinery, but the review system is already rubric-parameterised: `reckon/crew/review.py:175` defines `PLAN_REVIEW_RUBRICS`, `:359 load_plan_review_prompt`, `:628` maps rubric to item list, and `:687 parse_plan_review_report` parses a second role's report; `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` (988 lines) is the existing sibling role. A census of §6's uncited prior art: (1) role/prompt/parser reuse `reckon/crew/review.py:175,359,628,687`; (2) sibling role module `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`; (3) image-input lane capability `reckon/_flight_schema.py:294` and its refusal in `reckon/flight.py:1381` (`select_profile_backend`). The plan cites none of the three, so an implementer reads §6 as greenfield.

findings.reason: a parallel module for a new rubric is surface without depth; the honest change is a fourth rubric in the existing parameterised role, exactly as `plan_review` was added, and the plan should either extend it or justify the fork.
findings.text: §6 introduces a new module and prompt for one review role whose only distinct behaviour is a trigger (diff touches a figures image), a prompt, a caption-only write scope, and a lane requirement — all of which the existing role mechanism already expresses (rubric selection plus prompt file at `reckon/crew/review.py:354-359`, one write-scope rule, one capability check). The section never says why `review.py`'s role parameter cannot carry a figure rubric.

findings.reason: without naming `_flight_schema.input_modalities` and `routing.select_profile_backend`, §6's implementer will add a second capability check that drifts from the one the gate already verified.
findings.text: §6's requirement that "a figure review refuses a lane that cannot read an image" duplicates an owner that already ships: `reckon/_flight_schema.py:294` declares `input_modalities` ("a lane that does not say it reads images is treated as not reading them"), and `reckon/crew/routing.py:select_profile_backend` performs the refusal — recorded by this plan's own closed gate `g-ssp-figure-lane` (`plan.html:3231-3234`, evidence `a-review-can-see-the-figure#s1`), which states §6 "must route through select_profile_backend". The §6 body text does not name that owner, and re-derives figure detection that `reckon/figures.py` (`figure_rows` at `reckon/figures.py:116`) owns.

findings.reason: each added family must be accounted for in the section's own text, or the plan grows interface surface the budget counts without a stated offset.
findings.text: with public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33 and refusal_families 23, §6 adds a public module (`figure_review.py`), a prompt file, a new role and a new refusal family, and states nothing it retires or merges nor why nothing can be; §12 likewise proposes a `--dispatch-reviews` option (`reckon/cli.py:6951`) in its remedy list without naming what it retires.

findings.reason: §11 retires a printed command in the armed case, which satisfies the "names what it retires" rule rather than breaking it.
findings.text: §11 changes the review-missing obligation from "prints the dispatch command" to "prints it only when no armed follower will dispatch", which narrows a surface rather than adding one, and names the owner (`crew complete` obligation text); this is the correct shape and is recorded here as the census's negative instance so the accounting is not read as blank.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan's substantive mechanisms are extensions of existing deep modules (promotion refusal into `reckon/crew/promotion.py`, the reflex into `resumption.sweep`, the store index into `reckon/crew/review.py`, ledger shrink-refusal into `reckon/ledger.py`); no proposed module hides less than it exposes.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6 re-declares the "a lane can read an image" capability and its dispatch refusal, which is already owned by `reckon/_flight_schema.py:294` (`input_modalities`) and `reckon/flight.py:1381` (`select_profile_backend`), and re-derives figure detection owned by `reckon/figures.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §6 adds a module, a prompt and a refusal family, and §12 adds a `--dispatch-reviews` CLI option, none of which the sections account for by naming what they retire or merge, or stating why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searches the code it extends across §1–§5 and cites file:line throughout, but §6 proposes a figure-review role without citing the review module's existing rubric-parameterised roles (`reckon/crew/review.py:175` `PLAN_REVIEW_RUBRICS`, `:359 load_plan_review_prompt`, `:687 parse_plan_review_report`) or the sibling role module `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`, and without citing the image-input declaration it depends on (`reckon/_flight_schema.py:294` `input_modalities`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §6 adds a new module `reckon/crew/figure_review.py` plus a new prompt for a review role, over a review module that already parameterises role, prompt and parser by rubric, without stating why the existing role mechanism cannot be extended.
